neighbours.label: Fires on prepositions (in, of) that link an abstract emotional or spiritual noun to its scope in uplifting, inspirational prose (light in the darkness, joy in the little things, the midst of trouble); quiet on the same prepositions in technical or factual prose.
fire: Grandma always taught us to find joy in the smallest things.
His courage in the face of loss inspired the whole town.
May you find peace in the storms that life brings your way.
Their story is a reminder of the power of hope and kindness.
Even on hard days, there is beauty in the struggle to grow.
She carried a spark of faith through the darkest winter.
We celebrate the strength of the human spirit in every child.
Look for the good in people, and you will find it everywhere.
quiet: Grandma always taught us to store flour in the smallest jars.
The cracks in the face of the dam were repaired last year.
The pumps were installed in the basement before the storm.

Even on hot days, there is water in the tank on the roof.
She carried a box of files through the main office corridor.
We measured the strength of the steel samples in every batch.
Look for the label on the box, and you will find the code.
